section_1.title: Introduction: The Privacy Paradox
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Define the goal of DP-3T (Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing): notification without central identification.
section_1.example: Characters Alice and Bob sit on a park bench. They want to know if they've been exposed to a virus later, but they don't want a central server to know they met or where they were.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Cryptographic Hash Functions & BLE
section_2.content: Explain two building blocks: 1. Hash Functions (One-way 'digital blenders' that turn data into unique fingerprints). 2. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) (Short-range radio 'beacons' that act like a digital handshake).
section_2.example: An animation of a 'Hash Machine' turning a secret word into a complex code that cannot be reversed. A visualization of Bob's phone emitting a faint blue pulse that only reaches Alice's phone 2 meters away.

section_3.title: Local Identity Generation: The Rotating IDs
section_3.content: Explain the hierarchy of keys: The Secret Day Key (SK) and the Rolling Proximity Identifiers (RPI). Use a graphical representation: SK_t -> [Hash] -> RPI_1, RPI_2... RPI_n. Emphasize that RPIs change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
section_3.example: Alice's phone generates a 'Master Key' for the day. From this, it creates 'Temporary Business Cards' (RPIs). Just like a chameleon changing colors, Alice's digital ID looks different to every person she passes throughout the day.

section_4.title: The Digital Handshake: Proximity Exchange
section_4.content: When Alice and Bob are near, their phones exchange and store only the RPIs they heard. Crucially, this data stays *on the phone*, not on a server. Mathematically, the local log is a set: L = {RPI_received, timestamp, signal_strength}.
section_4.example: Alice and Bob's phones 'whisper' their current 15-minute IDs to each other. Alice's phone saves Bob's random code 'X8j2' but has no idea it belongs to 'Bob'.

section_5.title: Infection Reporting: The Decentralized Upload
section_5.content: If Bob tests positive, he uploads his Secret Day Keys (SK) for the infectious period to a central 'Bulletin Board.' He does NOT upload his contact list. The server only sees a list of 'Sick Keys' but doesn't know who Bob met.
section_5.example: Bob's doctor gives him a code. Bob's phone sends his 'Master Keys' to a public cloud. The cloud server acts like a public notice board in a town square where anyone can read, but the board doesn't know who is reading it.

section_6.title: Local Risk Assessment: The Matching Process
section_6.content: Every phone (including Alice's) periodically downloads the 'Sick Keys.' Alice's phone locally regenerates the RPIs from those keys and compares them with its own 'Heard IDs' log. If there's a match, the phone alerts the user.
section_6.example: A visual split-screen: On the left, Alice's phone downloads Bob's 'Master Key'. It runs the 'Hash Machine' to see all IDs Bob used. On the right, it compares them to Alice's 'Heard IDs'. A 'Match Found!' pop-up appears only on Alice's screen.

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_7.content: Review the core strengths: 1. Decentralization (Matches happen on-device). 2. Ephemeral IDs (Prevention of tracking). 3. Privacy by Design (The server is 'blind').
section_7.example: A summary graphic showing a shield protecting Alice's identity while a warning bell rings, symbolizing that she is safe and informed simultaneously.

section_1.title: Introduction: The Privacy Paradox
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Define the goal of DP-3T (Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing): notification without central identification.
section_1.example: Characters Alice and Bob sit on a park bench. They want to know if they've been exposed to a virus later, but they don't want a central server to know they met or where they were.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Cryptographic Hash Functions & BLE
section_2.content: Explain two building blocks: 1. Hash Functions (One-way 'digital blenders' that turn data into unique fingerprints). 2. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) (Short-range radio 'beacons' that act like a digital handshake).
section_2.example: An animation of a 'Hash Machine' turning a secret word into a complex code that cannot be reversed. A visualization of Bob's phone emitting a faint blue pulse that only reaches Alice's phone 2 meters away.

section_3.title: Local Identity Generation: The Rotating IDs
section_3.content: Explain the hierarchy of keys: The Secret Day Key (SK) and the Rolling Proximity Identifiers (RPI). Use a graphical representation: SK_t -> [Hash] -> RPI_1, RPI_2... RPI_n. Emphasize that RPIs change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
section_3.example: Alice's phone generates a 'Master Key' for the day. From this, it creates 'Temporary Business Cards' (RPIs). Just like a chameleon changing colors, Alice's digital ID looks different to every person she passes throughout the day.

section_4.title: The Digital Handshake: Proximity Exchange
section_4.content: When Alice and Bob are near, their phones exchange and store only the RPIs they heard. Crucially, this data stays *on the phone*, not on a server. Mathematically, the local log is a set: L = {RPI_received, timestamp, signal_strength}.
section_4.example: Alice and Bob's phones 'whisper' their current 15-minute IDs to each other. Alice's phone saves Bob's random code 'X8j2' but has no idea it belongs to 'Bob'.

section_5.title: Infection Reporting: The Decentralized Upload
section_5.content: If Bob tests positive, he uploads his Secret Day Keys (SK) for the infectious period to a central 'Bulletin Board.' He does NOT upload his contact list. The server only sees a list of 'Sick Keys' but doesn't know who Bob met.
section_5.example: Bob's doctor gives him a code. Bob's phone sends his 'Master Keys' to a public cloud. The cloud server acts like a public notice board in a town square where anyone can read, but the board doesn't know who is reading it.

section_6.title: Local Risk Assessment: The Matching Process
section_6.content: Every phone (including Alice's) periodically downloads the 'Sick Keys.' Alice's phone locally regenerates the RPIs from those keys and compares them with its own 'Heard IDs' log. If there's a match, the phone alerts the user.
section_6.example: A visual split-screen: On the left, Alice's phone downloads Bob's 'Master Key'. It runs the 'Hash Machine' to see all IDs Bob used. On the right, it compares them to Alice's 'Heard IDs'. A 'Match Found!' pop-up appears only on Alice's screen.

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_7.content: Review the core strengths: 1. Decentralization (Matches happen on-device). 2. Ephemeral IDs (Prevention of tracking). 3. Privacy by Design (The server is 'blind').
section_7.example: A summary graphic showing a shield protecting Alice's identity while a warning bell rings, symbolizing that she is safe and informed simultaneously.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Local Identity Generation: The Rotating IDs"
        lines = [
            "Each phone generates a secret daily master key.",
            "Hash functions derive temporary IDs from the master key.",
            "These ephemeral IDs change every fifteen minutes.",
            "Rotating IDs prevent tracking a user over time.",
            "All identity generation happens strictly on your device."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_SK = "#F39C12"
        COLOR_RPI1 = "#1ABC9C"
        COLOR_RPI2 = "#16A085"
        COLOR_RPI3 = "#138D75"
        COLOR_GREY = "#BDC3C7"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A golden 'Secret Key' (SK) (#F39C12) appears.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SK)
        sk_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=COLOR_SK, fill_opacity=0.2)
        sk_text = Text("Secret Key (SK)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_SK)
        sk_group = VGroup(sk_box, sk_text)
        self.place_at_grid(sk_group, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sk_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Arrow from SK to three 'RPI' boxes.
        # RPI_1 (#1ABC9C), RPI_2 (#16A085), RPI_3 (#138D75) appear.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_RPI1)
        
        rpi1_box = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_RPI1, fill_opacity=0.2)
        rpi1_text = Text("RPI_1", font_size=18, color=COLOR_RPI1)
        rpi1 = VGroup(rpi1_box, rpi1_text)
        self.place_at_grid(rpi1, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)

        rpi2_box = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_RPI2, fill_opacity=0.2)
        rpi2_text = Text("RPI_2", font_size=18, color=COLOR_RPI2)
        rpi2 = VGroup(rpi2_box, rpi2_text)
        self.place_at_grid(rpi2, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)

        rpi3_box = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.6, color=COLOR_RPI3, fill_opacity=0.2)
        rpi3_text = Text("RPI_3", font_size=18, color=COLOR_RPI3)
        rpi3 = VGroup(rpi3_box, rpi3_text)
        self.place_at_grid(rpi3, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)

        arrow1 = Arrow(sk_group.get_bottom(), rpi1.get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(sk_group.get_bottom(), rpi2.get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        arrow3 = Arrow(sk_group.get_bottom(), rpi3.get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        
        hash_label = Text("Hash", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(hash_label, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2), Create(arrow3), Write(hash_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(rpi1), FadeIn(rpi2), FadeIn(rpi3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Clock icon (#BDC3C7) spins; RPI_1 fades, RPI_2 glows.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_GREY)
        
        clock_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color=COLOR_GREY)
        clock_hand1 = Line(clock_circle.get_center(), clock_circle.get_top() * 0.7 + clock_circle.get_center() * 0.3, color=COLOR_GREY)
        clock_hand2 = Line(clock_circle.get_center(), clock_circle.get_right() * 0.5 + clock_circle.get_center() * 0.5, color=COLOR_GREY)
        clock = VGroup(clock_circle, clock_hand1, clock_hand2)
        self.place_at_grid(clock, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(clock))
        self.play(
            Rotate(clock_hand1, angle=-2*PI, about_point=clock_circle.get_center()),
            Rotate(clock_hand2, angle=-4*PI, about_point=clock_circle.get_center()),
            rpi1.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            rpi2.animate.set_stroke(width=6).set_fill(opacity=0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Rotating IDs prevent tracking a user over time.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_RPI2)
        
        # Visualize "rotation" by fading rpi2 and highlighting rpi3
        self.play(
            rpi2.animate.set_opacity(0.3).set_stroke(width=2).set_fill(opacity=0.2),
            rpi3.animate.set_stroke(width=6).set_fill(opacity=0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # A border (#BDC3C7) surrounds the key and IDs, labeled 'Local Device'.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_GREY)
        
        # Define the area for the device boundary
        device_border = RoundedRectangle(
            width=5.5, 
            height=5.0, 
            corner_radius=0.3, 
            color=COLOR_GREY, 
            stroke_dash_array=[8, 8]
        )
        self.place_in_area(device_border, "A1", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        device_label = Text("Local Device", font_size=20, color=COLOR_GREY).next_to(device_border, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(device_border))
        self.play(Write(device_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: Cryptographic Hash Functions & BLE",
            [
                "Hash functions create unique, irreversible digital fingerprints.",
                "Bluetooth Low Energy enables short-range device discovery.",
                "These tools form the foundation of privacy-preserving tracing."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Hash Function box transforms text to hex code.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        hash_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.5, width=3, color="#A569BD", fill_opacity=0.2)
        hash_label = Text("Hash Function", font_size=24, color="#A569BD")
        hash_group = VGroup(hash_box, hash_label)
        self.place_in_area(hash_group, "B2", "C5")
        
        input_text = Text("Secret ID", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(input_text, "B1")
        
        output_hex = Text("8f3c...2a", font_size=20, color="#A569BD")
        self.place_at_grid(output_hex, "C6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(hash_group))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(input_text.animate.move_to(hash_box.get_center()), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(input_text, scale=0.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(output_hex, shift=RIGHT), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        pulses = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=r, stroke_color=pulse_color, stroke_opacity=1 - (r/3))

        ]).move_to(phone_1.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(phone_1))
        
        # Animate pulses with ValueTracker for performance and smoothness
        pulse_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_pulses(p_group):
            val = pulse_tracker.get_value()
            for i, p in enumerate(p_group):
                # Offset each pulse
                offset_val = (val + i * 0.33) % 1.0
                new_radius = 0.2 + offset_val * 2.5
                p.set_width(new_radius * 2)
                p.set_stroke(opacity=1 - offset_val)

        pulses.add_updater(update_pulses)
        self.add(pulses)
        self.play(pulse_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        phone_2 = VGroup(phone_2_body, phone_2_screen)
        self.place_at_grid(phone_2, "E6") # Start at E6
        
        check_mark = Tex(r"\checkmark", color="#2ECC71", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(check_mark, "D5")
        check_mark.shift(UP * 0.5) # Positioning relative to phone 2 destination

        self.play(phone_2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]), run_time=2)
        
        # When phone 2 enters radius (D5 is approx 3 units from D2)
        self.play(Write(check_mark))
        self.play(pulse_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

section_1.title: Introduction: The Privacy Paradox
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Define the goal of DP-3T (Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing): notification without central identification.
section_1.example: Characters Alice and Bob sit on a park bench. They want to know if they've been exposed to a virus later, but they don't want a central server to know they met or where they were.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Cryptographic Hash Functions & BLE
section_2.content: Explain two building blocks: 1. Hash Functions (One-way 'digital blenders' that turn data into unique fingerprints). 2. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) (Short-range radio 'beacons' that act like a digital handshake).
section_2.example: An animation of a 'Hash Machine' turning a secret word into a complex code that cannot be reversed. A visualization of Bob's phone emitting a faint blue pulse that only reaches Alice's phone 2 meters away.

section_3.title: Local Identity Generation: The Rotating IDs
section_3.content: Explain the hierarchy of keys: The Secret Day Key (SK) and the Rolling Proximity Identifiers (RPI). Use a graphical representation: SK_t -> [Hash] -> RPI_1, RPI_2... RPI_n. Emphasize that RPIs change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
section_3.example: Alice's phone generates a 'Master Key' for the day. From this, it creates 'Temporary Business Cards' (RPIs). Just like a chameleon changing colors, Alice's digital ID looks different to every person she passes throughout the day.

section_4.title: The Digital Handshake: Proximity Exchange
section_4.content: When Alice and Bob are near, their phones exchange and store only the RPIs they heard. Crucially, this data stays *on the phone*, not on a server. Mathematically, the local log is a set: L = {RPI_received, timestamp, signal_strength}.
section_4.example: Alice and Bob's phones 'whisper' their current 15-minute IDs to each other. Alice's phone saves Bob's random code 'X8j2' but has no idea it belongs to 'Bob'.

section_5.title: Infection Reporting: The Decentralized Upload
section_5.content: If Bob tests positive, he uploads his Secret Day Keys (SK) for the infectious period to a central 'Bulletin Board.' He does NOT upload his contact list. The server only sees a list of 'Sick Keys' but doesn't know who Bob met.
section_5.example: Bob's doctor gives him a code. Bob's phone sends his 'Master Keys' to a public cloud. The cloud server acts like a public notice board in a town square where anyone can read, but the board doesn't know who is reading it.

section_6.title: Local Risk Assessment: The Matching Process
section_6.content: Every phone (including Alice's) periodically downloads the 'Sick Keys.' Alice's phone locally regenerates the RPIs from those keys and compares them with its own 'Heard IDs' log. If there's a match, the phone alerts the user.
section_6.example: A visual split-screen: On the left, Alice's phone downloads Bob's 'Master Key'. It runs the 'Hash Machine' to see all IDs Bob used. On the right, it compares them to Alice's 'Heard IDs'. A 'Match Found!' pop-up appears only on Alice's screen.

section_7.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_7.content: Review the core strengths: 1. Decentralization (Matches happen on-device). 2. Ephemeral IDs (Prevention of tracking). 3. Privacy by Design (The server is 'blind').
section_7.example: A summary graphic showing a shield protecting Alice's identity while a warning bell rings, symbolizing that she is safe and informed simultaneously.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class TeachingScene(Scene):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Bulletin Board (Source of Keys)

        board = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=3.0, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)

        self.place_at_grid(board, 'B4')

        # Keys Downloading
        key_1 = Square(side_length=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=KEY_COLOR)
        key_2 = Square(side_length=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=KEY_COLOR)
        key_3 = Square(side_length=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=KEY_COLOR)

        self.place_at_grid(keys, 'B4')

        self.lecture[0].set_color(KEY_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(alice_phone), Create(phone_label), Create(board), Create(board_label))
        # Move keys to center of phone (D4)
        self.play(keys.animate.move_to(self.grid['D4']))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        rpi_1 = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=RPI_COLOR)
        rpi_2 = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=RPI_COLOR)
        rpi_3 = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=RPI_COLOR)
        rpis = VGroup(rpi_1, rpi_2, rpi_3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        # Resolution for Issue 48: Placement in center column (D4)
        self.place_at_grid(rpis, 'D4')

        self.lecture[1].set_color(RPI_COLOR)
        self.play(Transform(keys, rpis))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        local_log_box = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=1.2, color=LOG_COLOR)

        local_log = VGroup(local_log_box, log_title.next_to(local_log_box, UP, buff=0.1), log_entry_1, log_entry_2, log_entry_3)
        
        # Position log inside phone (left column D3)

        # Move RPIs to the right side inside phone (D5) to avoid overlapping with log

        # Comparison indicator: Spans columns 3 to 5 (phone width)

        alert_text = Text("RISK ALERT", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        alert_group = VGroup(alert_box, alert_text)

        self.play(FadeIn(alert_group, shift=UP))
